transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. Um... I'm not entirely sure how to explain this without sounding, well, I don't want you to think badly of me. I want to be as helpful as possible. 

It's just... I'm here because of my house. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, a simple issue with paperwork and missed payments. And I know how that sounds on the surface, I really do. But... I've been noticing things. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my retail job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like a lot to take in. But no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing happening for almost two years now. Is... is it okay that I share that with you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and answering your question properly.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people around you could not?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I promise I don't have anything like that happening. 

I know the things I was just saying about the bank and my job might make it seem like I'm... well, I really hope you don't think I'm imagining things. I've never heard voices or seen anything that isn't actually there. I would tell you if I did, I want to be completely honest with you. 

Everything I've noticed—the way my coworkers look at me, the specific wording in the letters from the loan servicer—it's all real, physical things that anyone could see if they just knew what to look for. I'm just very observant, I guess. 

I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression of me. Does... does that answer your question okay? I can explain it differently if you need me to.
Have you had a period of at least one week where you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep than usual?

Oh, um, no. No, I haven't had anything like that. I've always been a pretty good sleeper, honestly. I try really hard to keep a regular schedule, you know, so I can be at my best for work and... well, just to stay healthy. 

I definitely don't get unusually energized or irritable. I mean, the stress with the house and everything has been exhausting, but I don't get manic or anything like that. I really try to keep my emotions in check and stay professional, especially with everything going on. 

I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I've been doing. I'm trying my best to be helpful.
Have you noticed any times when your thoughts or speech become hard for other people to follow?

Oh, no, I don't think so. Um... I try very hard to speak clearly and make sure people understand me. I mean, sometimes when I'm trying to explain all the connections I've found—like the specific dates on the bank letters matching up with when my manager changes my schedule—people might look a little confused at first. But that's just because it's a lot of information, not because my thoughts are jumbled. 

Once I lay it all out for them, they can follow it just fine. I always make sure to organize my thoughts before I speak. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm not making sense, you know? 

I hope that answers your question? I just want to reassure you that I'm completely lucid and I try my best to communicate well. Is there a better way I could explain that?
Do you believe anything else unusual is happening to you besides the foreclosure and people at work?

No, no, nothing else. Just... just what I've told you about the bank and my coworkers. 

I mean, that's more than enough to deal with, right? I'm really just a normal person trying to handle a very stressful situation. I don't have any, um, bizarre theories or anything like that. I just want to keep my head down, do my job, and save my house. 

I really hope I don't sound like I'm complaining too much, or making a big deal out of nothing. I know you must see people with much bigger problems. I'm just trying to be thorough so you understand my situation. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.
Is it possible that the foreclosure is happening for ordinary financial reasons, even if it feels unlikely to you?

Oh, um... I know it probably sounds like that to most people. And I really, really wish it were just ordinary financial reasons, I do. That would be so much easier to fix, wouldn't it? Just... catch up on payments and it all goes away. 

But... well, everyone keeps acting like it's just paperwork and missed payments. They show me all these documents, but... I know what I've been seeing for almost two years now. It's not just a coincidence that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job are all... well, quietly working together. It's like they're trying to push me out of my house. 

I know that sounds bad, and I really don't want to seem like I'm not taking responsibility for my finances or anything. I just... no amount of papers they show me changes what's actually happening. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult or stubborn? I'm really trying to be reasonable about all this, I promise. I just have to be honest about what I'm experiencing. Is it okay that I see it that way?
Has anything else ever made you think people, organizations, or outside forces are specifically targeting or controlling you?

Oh, no, no. Nothing like that. Um... I really don't think there are any outside forces or, you know, secret organizations controlling me or anything. That sounds like something out of a movie, doesn't it? 

I just... I just have this very specific issue with the bank and the people at work, and that's all. I don't feel like I'm being targeted by anyone else or anything bigger than that. I'm completely in control of myself and my own choices. 

I hope I'm making it clear that I'm just a regular person dealing with a very difficult, very real situation. I wouldn't want you to think I have wild ideas about being controlled or anything. That's... that's not me at all. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
How certain are you that the bank and your coworkers are targeting you — could you be mistaken, or are you completely convinced it’s true?

I... I know it's hard for other people to understand. And I really, really wish I could say I was mistaken. It would be so much easier, wouldn't it? If I could just say, "Oh, I misunderstood, it's just normal paperwork." 

But... I'm completely sure. I've been seeing this happen for almost two years now. Everyone keeps acting like it's just missed payments, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've watched it happen. No amount of papers they show me changes what I've actually experienced. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound unreasonable or... or crazy. I know how it must sound to you, and I hate that I have to insist on it. I just have to be honest about what I know is true. Is it okay that I'm that certain? I'm just trying to give you the honest truth about my situation.
Have you ever had a major depressive episode, with at least two weeks of feeling very sad or losing interest in things?

Oh, um... no. No, I haven't. I mean, obviously, this whole situation with the house has been... well, a little stressful, as you can imagine. But I definitely haven't been sitting around feeling hopeless or losing interest in my life or anything like that. 

I actually try really hard to stay positive. I still go to work every day and do my best as a supervisor, even with everything going on behind the scenes there. I'm not the kind of person to just give up on things or get completely down. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want you to know I'm really doing my best to handle everything as normally and responsibly as possible. I wouldn't want you to think I was letting myself fall apart. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Have you ever believed that something impossible or highly unusual was happening to you, like your thoughts being put into or taken out of your mind, or your body being controlled by someone else?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. Um... I've never thought anyone was putting thoughts in my head or taking them out, or controlling my body. That really does sound like science fiction, doesn't it? 

I'm just a normal person, really. My thoughts are my own, and my body is my own. I know exactly what I'm thinking and doing. The only thing I'm dealing with is just... just the situation with the bank and the people at work, like I mentioned. It's just a real-world problem, nothing strange or impossible like mind control. 

I really want to reassure you that I don't have any thoughts like that. I'm completely grounded in reality, I promise. I hope I'm answering these questions right? I just want to make sure you see that I'm completely rational, just... just going through a tough time with my mortgage.
Do you think the bank and your coworkers are using any kind of secret technology or supernatural power to target you?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. Um, I don't believe in anything like that—secret technology or supernatural powers. That sounds... well, that sounds a bit crazy, doesn't it? 

I know it's just regular people doing regular, sneaky things. It's just emails, phone calls, manipulating the paperwork... very normal, mundane ways of messing with someone. There's no magic or sci-fi gadgets involved at all. I wouldn't ever think something like that. 

I just want to be really clear that I'm completely level-headed about how they're doing this. It's just a coordinated effort, nothing supernatural. Does that make sense? I hope I'm showing you that I'm looking at this in a very practical, realistic way.
Has this belief about the bank and your coworkers been the only unusual belief you've had?

Um, yes. Well, I mean, I don't really think of the situation with the bank as an unusual belief, if I'm being completely honest. It's just a very difficult reality I'm trying to manage. But to answer your question... no, there's absolutely nothing else. 

I don't have any other... strange ideas or anything like that. I just go to work, supervise my team, and try to keep everything running smoothly. I really hope you can see that I'm just a very regular, responsible person who's caught in a bad spot. 

I'm trying to be as open and helpful as I can with you... am I doing okay? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information and not coming across as someone who just imagines things.
Has this belief caused you to do worse at work or in your daily life?

Um, well... I'd like to think I'm still doing a really good job overall. I mean, when the foreclosure stuff isn't right in front of me, I'm completely fine. I still get up every morning, go in, supervise my team, handle the schedules, deal with customer issues... all the normal things a supervisor does. I take good care of myself, too. I really try to keep things professional and put together.

It's just... well, it only gets a little hard when the mail comes, or if the bank calls, or if I see paperwork at work that... that looks like it's tied to what they're doing with my house. That's when I get a bit distracted, I guess. But I really try not to let it affect my actual work performance. I'm still very dedicated to my job. I hope that makes sense? I just want you to know I'm still very capable and responsible, despite this... this awful situation they've put me in. Am I explaining that alright?

Outside of the foreclosure and work situation, would you say you generally get along with people and function normally, or have you had a long-standing pattern of feeling suspicious or odd in other areas too?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I really pride myself on being a people person. You know, you kind of have to be when you work in retail. I get along fine with everyone—my friends, my family, the neighbors. I've never been the type to be... well, suspicious of people in general. 

I really hope I don't come across that way to you. I just try to be friendly and helpful to everyone I meet. I've always just lived a very normal, quiet life before all this started happening with the house. I'm really not an odd person at all, and I've never had trouble trusting people before this. 

I hope you can see that? I just want to make sure you know I'm usually very easygoing and social. I'm doing my best to show you the kind of person I really am... is that helpful?
Have you ever had any experiences of hearing or seeing things that other people around you did not, even once?

Oh, no. No, never anything like that. I've never heard voices or seen things that weren't there. I know some people struggle with those kinds of things, but I've honestly never had that happen to me, not even once. 

I really try to stay very grounded in reality, you know? My mind is perfectly clear, I promise. I just... I really want to make sure you know that I'm not... I'm not losing my mind or anything. I'm just a normal person dealing with a really stressful situation with the bank. 

I hope you believe me? I'm trying to be completely honest with you so you can see that I'm perfectly sane. I'm answering everything the right way, aren't I?
Have you ever had a period of at least one week where you felt unusually energized or irritable and needed much less sleep than usual?

No, I... I've never had anything like that. I've always been a very good sleeper, actually. I need my full eight hours to be at my best for work, you know? I've never gone days without sleep or felt... well, unusually wired or irritable like that. 

I really try to keep a steady routine. I go to bed at a reasonable hour, I wake up, I go to work... just very normal, everyday things. I don't want you to think I'm prone to extreme moods or anything. I'm usually very even-keeled. 

Even with all this stress about the house, I still make sure I get my rest so I can function properly. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to reassure you that I'm taking good care of myself and keeping things as normal as possible. Does that sound like what you're looking for?
Have other people told you that you seem emotionally flat, distant, or less expressive than usual?

Oh, no, I... I don't think anyone has ever said that about me. If anything, I'm usually the one who's very... well, very expressive and engaged. Working as a supervisor, you really have to be warm and present for your team and the customers, you know? 

I certainly don't want to come across as cold or distant to anyone. I always try to smile and make sure people know I'm listening to them and that I care about what they're saying. I haven't felt flat at all, and my friends or coworkers haven't mentioned anything like that to me. 

I... I hope I'm coming across as warm to you, too? I'm really trying to be as open and cooperative as I can be here. I wouldn't want you to think I was shutting down or anything. Does that make sense?
Have you ever been told that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from topic to topic in a way that makes it difficult for others to understand?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've always prided myself on being a very clear communicator. In retail, especially as a supervisor, you really have to be able to explain things logically and keep everyone on the same page, right? 

I always make sure I finish my thoughts and stay focused on whatever we're discussing. I would hate it if people thought I was rambling or confusing them. No one at work or in my personal life has ever complained about my speech. I try to be very articulate. 

I mean, I hope I'm making sense to you right now? I'm really trying to answer your questions as directly as possible so you have exactly what you need. I'm doing okay with that, aren't I?
Have you ever had a period of at least one week where you felt unusually upbeat or euphoric?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have good days, of course—everyone has days where they feel happy and positive, right? But never anything unusual or... euphoric, like you said. 

I really try to keep a level head. Being a supervisor, you can't afford to be too high or too low; you have to be the stable one for everyone else. So I've never had a whole week where I was acting out of character or overly upbeat. Just normal happiness when things are going well. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of information you need to see that I'm, you know, very stable. I haven't given you any reason to think otherwise, have I?
